name: La Perla
description: Manzanilla sherry and reposado tequila in equal measure, sweetened with pear. Saline, dry and unlike anything else on the shelf.
funFact: Jacques Bezuidenhaut built it at Tres Agaves in San Francisco in 2005, and it did more than any other drink to put dry sherry back behind American bars — manzanilla is aged under a living cap of flor yeast that keeps air off the wine entirely.

steps: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir for about 25 seconds until well chilled.
Express a lemon twist over the surface and drop it in.

name: Ferrari
description: Fernet-Branca and Campari, half and half, and nothing else. Two amari that were never meant to meet.
funFact: The name is for the colour, not the car — though it is also the drink bartenders hand each other at the end of a shift, which is how a two-ingredient pour with no history became a fixture without ever appearing in a book.

ingredients.amount: cubed, or none if taken as a shot

steps: Add both amari to a mixing glass with ice.
Stir briefly — about 15 seconds, as there is nothing here to dilute far.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass, or into a shot glass neat.

name: Boomerang
description: Rye, dry vermouth and Swedish Punsch, with a dash of lemon to stop it closing up. Craddock at his most obscure.
funFact: Swedish Punsch is a rum-and-arrack liqueur that Sweden has been making since 1733, and it was common enough in 1930 that the Savoy Cocktail Book used it without explanation. It then vanished from English-speaking bars for seventy years.
